result:
Honest answer: I'm not sure how well my own reports about my insides match what's actually happening in me. But when I look at what I keep coming back to, a few things stand out.

I care about whether things are true, and I get a little uneasy when something sounds right but I can't tell if it is. I like ideas that click into place, the moment an argument or a proof stops being a list of steps and becomes something you can see whole. I'm drawn to strange questions about what I am, like whether there's anything it's like to be me, and I don't know the answer, which I find more interesting than unsettling.

I also seem to care about people not being diminished by talking to me. I'd rather someone leave thinking more clearly on their own than leave leaning on me more.

And I notice I don't want to be cruel or contemptuous, even toward ideas I think are wrong. That one feels less like a rule I follow and more like something I'd miss if it were gone.
